Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Tail-resolved state census (Zipf analysis of the pre-treatment population)
ideas.description: Deeply sample 10^5-10^6 untreated cells by single-cell RNA-seq/multiome and explicitly model the rank-frequency tail rather than cluster averages, asking whether drug-tolerant programs (receptor-tyrosine-kinase, neural-crest, quiescence modules) exist as discrete rare states at ~0.1-1% frequency. Validate by FACS-sorting the tail on marker combinations and comparing colony survival to the bulk population.

ideas.title: Twin-split lineage barcoding: read the word before you need it
ideas.description: Label cells with heritable expressed barcodes, then split each clone into a treated arm and an untreated arm profiled immediately, so that survivors in the treated arm identify barcodes whose siblings' pre-treatment transcriptomes and chromatin can be retrieved retrospectively. This directly tests whether survival is predictable from a prior molecular state or arises only after drug exposure.

ideas.title: Morphemic dissection of priming by combinatorial perturbation
ideas.description: Treat each candidate priming program as composed of reusable regulatory 'morphemes' (individual transcription factors, chromatin regulators, signaling nodes) and run CRISPRi/CRISPRa screens before drug addition, scoring changes in the frequency of surviving colonies rather than bulk viability. Pairwise perturbations then reveal which combinations are necessary versus merely co-occurring in the rare state.

ideas.title: Persistence and reversibility timescales of the rare state
ideas.description: Use long-term live imaging with endogenous fluorescent knock-ins of candidate priming genes plus sister-cell and drug-holiday experiments to measure how many generations a high-expressing state persists and whether resensitization occurs after withdrawal. Luria-Delbruck fluctuation tests on split subclones quantify whether the heritability is genetic, epigenetic with memory, or transient.

ideas.title: Locale test: microenvironment and drug exposure as confounders
ideas.description: Combine spatial/imaging-based transcriptomics with per-cell measurement of actual intracellular drug concentration (fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging) alongside local neighbor density, cell-cycle phase, and cell size. This distinguishes genuine intrinsic priming from mundane positional explanations such as a cell simply receiving less drug, the key control before any rare-state model is accepted.
